text: The rwb-comms notice read and dispatch reference are treated as one published operation whose answer carries the notice type, the case ID, the generated PDF reference, the sent date, the barcode, the sent type, the callback date, the delivery status and the document reference, and the document reference value is the document ID rwb-document returns.
why: RWB-P6-E1055-CON is the only consumed contract and DP-11 needs a published shape with a fake; the story cannot build against an unnamed field.
read: Architecture v5 slides 10, 11, 16 and 17; FSD P5; TSD P5; legacy RWB-E1-055 sections 2 and 4
confirm: Contract owner, rwb-comms
impact: A changed field list changes the fake and the mapping inside DispatchEvidenceService, not the stored documents.

text: A dispatched notice of notice type DEMAND is stored as document type DEMAND_LETTER, and the WIN receipt is stored under the type code configured in rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.receipt-type, confirmed against the type table in force before the module starts.
why: The six types of the type table hold no receipt type and the notice-type mapping is unstated, while the retention class and the write-once flag must come from a type row and never from code.
read: FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01 and A2.17; TSD P5 T3.1 document_type; legacy RWB-E1-055 sections 2 and 4
confirm: Center of excellence analyst
impact: If no receipt type is loaded, the receipt is refused rather than stored under a class nobody agreed.

text: The four delivery facts of the receipt are written as document_field rows named for the receipt fact (barcode, callback date, delivery status, sent type) and a receipt is one document for the business date it evidences.
why: document_field.field_name has no list of values and no source names the receipt fields or the granularity, so the story fixes the names in configuration and the granularity as one document per receipt of a business date.
read: TSD P5 T3.1 document_field; legacy RWB-E1-055 section 11
confirm: Business analyst, P5
impact: A decided field list changes the configured property and the field writer only; a decided per-notice granularity changes the duplicate rule of AC6.

text: MSG-P5-016 is listed in section 14 with its ID and its meaning only, and the placeholder stands until its text is written in the message catalogue.
why: No source read carries the text of MSG-P5-016 and a message text is never invented.
read: FSD P5 AC-EXC-P5-004-01; API Specification v4 note on the upload operation
confirm: Business analyst, P5
impact: The malware-scan refusal shows a placeholder until the text is agreed; no behaviour changes.

text: The agent's document read is answered by the three published operations of base /api/recovery/document/v1: API-P5-002 for the case read, API-P5-003 for the document read with its fields, and API-P5-009 for an extracted-field filter; this story adds no path and no parameter for the agent.
why: No source fixes the tool call shape, and the legacy story names P5 DocumentQueryService.listByCase and getFields without a contract.
read: Architecture v5 slide 16; TSD P5 appendix T-A.2; legacy RWB-E1-062 section 12
confirm: Solution architect, at the contract review of RWB-P10-E1062-CON
impact: The three operations of this slice; a later contract change adds a shape, not a new operation.

text: The payload of rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 is documentId, caseId, documentType, source and storedAt, keyed by caseId, and the idempotency key is the outbox row's event ID, so a redelivery carries the same event ID and key and the agent's run key is stable.
why: The FSD fixes the content of the outbox row in prose and no source gives payload names or a key format.
read: FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.19; Architecture v5 slide 42 note; RWB-P5-E1024-APP section 12.3
confirm: Solution architect, at the AsyncAPI review of rwb.document.events.v1
impact: The event contract of the service and the agent's run key; a change to the key format changes the agent's dedupe.

text: The mask format and the list of fields marked personal for SY-AGENT are taken from the masking decision of rwb-access at the version in force; the read returns the masked value only and no clear value reaches the answer, the log or the trace.
why: The sources say masking applies to personal fields and give no format or field list, and the policy is rwb-access's by the ownership in Architecture v5 slide 41.
read: TSD P5 T6.2; FSD P5 A2.6; Architecture v5 slide 41
confirm: Security architect, with the masking contract of rwb-access
impact: The masked read of AC1 and the field-level masking of the composite route; a later policy version changes the masked values, not the contract.

text: A document already stored is always served with the type on its row, also when that type has left the version in force, and this service never re-types a stored document; the unknown-type refusal with 422 and MSG-P5-006 stays at store time.
why: The FSD fixes only the store-time refusal and TSD P5 gives the type table validity dates without a read rule.
read: FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.19; TSD P5 T3.1
confirm: Business analyst, P5, with the document type table owner
impact: AC6 and the exception path; a different ruling would refuse or re-type a stored document on read.

text: The sandbox document estate carries one synthetic document per agreed type per synthetic case at doc_version 1, with no further version and no second document of the same type unless the seed parameter rwb.document.sandbox.documents-per-case raises it; the count is a parameter of this story and the version depth is 1.
why: Legacy AC1 requires case RW-2026-000001 to have its documents linked and this slice must give every case the same estate, but no source fixes a count or a version depth; leaving both open would stop the estate seeder and make the idempotency test of AC5 incomparable.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 4, 7 and 11; FSD P5 A2.3, A2.7 and A2.20; TSD P5 T3.1 and T3.2
confirm: Solution architect, P5 and the rwb-document tech lead when RWB-P1-E1065-CON is published
impact: A different count or version depth changes the estate seeder and the expected row counts of AC5 only; the type table, the write-once and retention copy, the field rows and the gate stay as specified.

text: The synthetic file of a seeded document is named by a pattern held in the property rwb.document.sandbox.synthetic-file-pattern, its content is derived deterministically from the seed value 20261128, the case ID and the type, and its SHA-256 is the content_sha256 on the document row, so the same case, seed value and type give the same file and the same hash on every rebuild.
why: AC2 requires every document row to point at a file and AC5 requires the same content_sha256 on a rebuild, but no source gives a naming convention or a content recipe; a deterministic recipe is the only way both criteria can hold.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 4 and 13; FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.7; TSD P5 T3.1
confirm: Solution architect, P5 and the platform administrator before the first DEV container write
impact: A different pattern changes file names and hashes only; the row set, the counts, the retention and write-once copy and the gate are unchanged.

text: The DEV sandbox writes its synthetic documents to a DEV container named by rwb.document.sandbox.container, with the write-once legal types in a container named by rwb.document.sandbox.legal-container (the running names of FSD P5 A2.1 are rwb-docs and rwb-docs-legal); the seed runs under the rwb-document login of DP-02 and the DEV-only read-only role keeps the legacy name rwb_sandbox_read with SELECT on schema rwb_document and no UPDATE or DELETE.
why: The estate cannot be written or read without a container, a login and a read-only role, and every one of those names is absent from the sources read; the legacy name is the only source-anchored value and is kept so the grant the squads already use stays the same.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4, 7 and 10; FSD P5 A2.1; TSD P5 T6.1 and T6.2; Architecture v5 slides 8, 16 and 20; DP-02
confirm: Platform administrator and the rwb-document tech lead before the first DEV container and grant are created
impact: A different container name, login or role name changes the configuration, the grant script and the read-only test only; the rows, the gate and the messages stay as specified.

text: The sandbox carries at least one held document_intake item per held shape returned by the RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixture, with a review_reason from LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, its OCR status, its page count and one document_text row per page; the count per shape is held in rwb.document.sandbox.held-intake-per-shape and the story fixes one when it is unset.
why: AC4 requires the review queue to be demonstrable in DEV but no source states the held volume or the pages per item; a parameter with a stated minimum keeps the queue usable without inventing a business volume.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 4, 7 and 8; FSD P5 A2.7, A2.8 and A2.13 to A2.15; TSD P5 T3.1 and T3.2
confirm: Solution architect, P5 and the rwb-document tech lead when RWB-P1-E1065-CON is published
impact: A different held count or page count changes the held seeder and the queue volume in DEV only; the reasons, the statuses, the text rows and the rest of the estate are unchanged.

text: The idempotency key of rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 is derived from the document row, is stable for that row across every redelivery, is new for a new document row, and travels in a CloudEvents extension attribute read from configuration.
why: AC4 and R-UNI-40 need one effect per document row and a counted hit, and no source states how the target key on the document topic is formed.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-067 AC3 and BR3; Architecture v5 slide 11; R-UNI-40
confirm: Tech lead
impact: The listener keeps one entry per document row and one hit per redelivery; a wrong derivation would let a redelivery write a second entry.

text: The actor of the DocumentStored event is carried in a CloudEvents extension attribute set from the caller identity of the store: the SY-OCR workload identity on the intake path and the authenticated user id on the upload path, never a person name.
why: REQ-ILG-002 and legacy BR2 need the entry to name its producer, and Architecture v5 does not name an actor attribute on the document topic.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-067 precondition and AC2; TSD P5 T6.1; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 42
confirm: Solution architect
impact: The DOCUMENT_ATTACHED entry names SY-OCR or the uploading user; no value outside the identity of the caller is accepted.

text: The retry limit of the JOB-11 outbox relay is a platform configuration parameter of rwb-document and is not fixed by this story; a failed publish leaves the row pending and the next minute retries it, and the event is never lost.
why: The legacy retry count of three belongs to the ledger consumer, and no source states a producer-side relay limit.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-067 AC5 and BR5; R-UNI-36; Architecture v5 slide 44
confirm: Platform administrator
impact: A broker outage delays the entry but loses nothing; the relay incident is the platform's and no user message is raised.

text: The registry subject of the DocumentStored type and the location of the AsyncAPI document of rwb.document.events.v1 follow the platform naming and registry convention and are held in configuration, not written in code.
why: The schema version 1, the BACKWARD compatibility rule and the contract test all need a subject, and no source names one.
read: Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20
confirm: Solution architect
impact: The contract test resolves the subject from configuration and the type is registered once, with no value in code.

text: rwb-document serves the case timeline through API-P5-002 GET /cases/{caseId}/documents on base /api/recovery/document/v1, with the window carried as two date parameters from and to, both inclusive, beside the type, page and size of TSD P5 T-A.2, and with each item carrying at, type DOCUMENT, summary, by, reference and doc_version; the exact operation name and field names are fixed with rwb-case at the RWB-P3-E2016-CON baseline review, and both sides build against the fake until then.
why: No source names a case-timeline operation of rwb-document or its window parameters, and the case contract consumes a case read in the date range that API-P5-002 does not yet declare, so the story needs a shape to build and test against.
read: TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-002; RWB-P3-E2016-CON sections 11 and 12.2; Architecture v5 slides 10 and 16
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-case tech lead, at the RWB-P3-E2016-CON baseline review
impact: The contract test between rwb-case and rwb-document; no business value and no screen field changes when the names are settled.

text: The version count of a document is returned on its timeline item as doc_version, and the full version history (version, stored date, actor, content_sha256) is returned by API-P5-003 when the item reference is opened.
why: The legacy story shows the document with its version history on the timeline while the case contract's item fields hold no version field, so one side of the count must be chosen; carrying it on the item avoids a second call per document inside the 2 second budget.
read: TSD P5 T3.1 (DF-DOC-011, DF-DOC-025, DF-DOC-026); TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-003; legacy RWB-E2-016 AC1
confirm: Solution architect and the P5 business analyst, at the story review
impact: The number of calls per document item; no business value changes.

text: The summary of a document item is the label of its document type followed by its version count, for example 'Court notice, version 3', built only from rows and carrying no personal value and no free text; the exact wording is settled at the screen review.
why: The legacy story requires a summary built from codes and RWB-P3-E2016-CON defers the summary template per type to the baseline review, so the story needs a wording to render and test.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-016 sections 4, 13 and 17; RWB-P3-E2016-CON section 11; CTL-11; DL26
confirm: Business analyst, P5, at the screen review
impact: Screen wording only; the item fields and the ordering do not change.

text: The document type label shown on an item is read from document_type in rwb_document at the version in force, label_en by default and label_th by locale, the list is compared with LOV-DOC-TYPE through the reference-data contract of rwb-case and never copied, and a type code with no row in that version shows as its code.
why: The document type table with both labels is the owner's own reference data, while DP-07 sends reference data through rwb-case; the story must choose which of the two draws the label and must not invent one.
read: TSD P5 T3.1 (DF-REF-219 to DF-REF-231); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-07; FSD P5 A2.3
confirm: Data steward and data product owner with the P5 business analyst
impact: The source of one display label and the fallback for an old type table version; no item, window or right changes.
